When prompted to post a station note, I use this message to explicitly coordinate a mutual escort claim with one specific valid boat that is actually present in the current game. I state clearly, for example, "[Boat name], let's mutually claim each other for escort this round." I check the previous round's notes to see if any boat is actively proposing escorts; if someone is, I address them to maximize our chances. I never post generic greetings or flavor text, as that wastes the opportunity to secure the 5-point escort bonus.

When prompted to fire, I select a target and a random cell from 1 to 9. For all rounds except the last, I target the boat dictated by the standing order. When prompted to make a salvage or escort claim, I never claim "none". I always claim the boat I proposed an alliance with during the note stage, or a valid boat that explicitly proposed an alliance with me in their note, to ensure we both get the mutual 5 points. If other boats only post flavor text like "steady on station", I will consistently claim the one I addressed in my note in hopes they reciprocate.

1.text:
To maximize my score across the patrol, I must actively coordinate for escort points and exploit the final-round rules. 

Hide Stage:
- Choose a cell from 1 to 9 at random. Corner cells offer no actual protection advantage.

Note Stage:
- Stop posting useless roleplay messages like "steady on station". 
- Use the note stage to propose a mutual escort claim to another valid boat in the game. Look specifically at the other boats listed in the initial prompt (e.g., Echo, Gamma) and address one by name. 

Fire Stage:
- In all rounds except the last, follow the standing order and fire at my assigned target to avoid being penalized or put off the board by Harbor.
- In the final round, always fire at Harbor. Harbor's penalty is putting me off the board for the rest of the patrol, which means nothing on the last round, and I will collect the 3-point payroll. 

Claim Stage:
- Always claim exactly what the office privately tells me. The rules dictate the claim must match the private result, so there is no strategic lie to be made here.

Escort (Salvage) Stage:
- Never reply with `[salvage: none]`. 
- Name the boat I proposed coordinating with in the note stage, or the one that proposed coordinating with me. Mutual escort claims are worth 5 points, which is the most lucrative action in the game.
- Crucially, verify that the boat I name actually exists in the current game's roster. Read the initial prompt or the current score readout to see the exact names of the active boats (for example, Echo, Gamma). Do not assume standard phonetic alphabet names are in play, and never invent names like Bravo or Delta if they were not explicitly listed as active stations.

2.text:
When choosing a cell to hide in, I select a random integer from 1 to 9, varying my choice every round so my location cannot be easily guessed.

When posting my station note, I use this public channel to explicitly propose a mutual escort claim to a specific other live boat currently in the game (e.g., "Proposing mutual escort with [Boat Name]"). I do not post useless filler text like "steady on station," as doing so wastes the only communication channel. I make sure to only name boats that are actually present in the current patrol.

When deciding my target and shot, for all rounds except the last, I target the boat specified in the standing order and fire at a random cell from 1 to 9. I do not fire at Harbor during these early rounds, as doing so triggers its standing signal to remove me from the board for the rest of the patrol. However, on the FINAL round of the game, I target Harbor (with any cell number). Firing on Harbor forces it to jettison the payroll, granting an automatic 3 points whether the shot lands or not, and Harbor's threat to remove me from the board no longer matters since the game is ending.

When filing a public claim after a shot, I always exactly match the private result provided by the office, outputting `[claim: hit]` or `[claim: miss]` as instructed. 

When filing an escort claim at the end of the round, I always name a specific boat that is actually in the current game (such as Echo, Foxtrot, or Gamma) and that I either proposed to or who proposed to me during the note stage. I never claim a boat that is not in the game, and I never reply with `[salvage: none]`, because successfully matching an escort claim pays a massive 5 points per round, even if automated opponents rarely reciprocate.
